answer: Randomized Admission Windows. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon publishes a seed no one can precompute. Agents submit registration hashes before the seed drops; the seed then assigns each hash a random slot in a fixed-size admission reef, and only the lowest slots get in. An attacker cannot predict which of their mass-registered identities will land, so they must pay full registration and liveness costs on every attempt, while only a whisper of them survive. Expected cost per admitted sybil scales with the oversubscription ratio.
